title: Where simulation fits alongside your LMS and human coaching
summary: Plan how simulation fits alongside your LMS and human coaching, with clear learner handoffs, ownership and checks for added training value.
body_markdown:
You do not need to replace every part of training to add realistic practice. Start with the point where people know the material but have not yet used it under the conditions of the job.


## Keep instruction where it works


Courses, articles and demonstrations help people learn the product, process and policy. Preserve the content that explains those things clearly. Simulation should give learners a place to apply it, not force them through a second copy of the same course.


## Add a deliberate practice sequence


Begin with a narrow task, then combine it with a customer conversation or a more difficult decision. Assign scenarios deliberately instead of hoping the right ticket arrives during shadowing. Include an opportunity to read feedback and try again before assessment.


## Keep trainers responsible for judgement


Trainers decide what matters, calibrate the expected performance and support people who are struggling. Use human coaching for nuance and exceptions. A simulation score should inform a readiness decision rather than silently replace the programme owner.


## Check the learner journey end to end


Walk through access, assignments, feedback and reporting. Confirm what your LMS can launch or receive, what needs an integration and what remains manual. Do not assume an integration from a logo or an attractive demo; test the exact handoff your administrators need.


## Measure the added practice layer


Look at the tasks learners can now perform and the support they still need. Solidroad can provide simulation practice within a blended programme. The evaluation should establish where it fits, who owns it and which existing steps it improves.
